# MK GitFlow

> An interactive, local-first platform for learning and working with Git. It
> lets you simulate Git commands on a visual branch graph before running them for
> real, backed by guided tutorials, a risk-graded command reference, deterministic
> utilities, an optional AI assistant, and a public repository analyzer.

Core principle: the site NEVER executes shell or Git commands. The simulator runs
a Git graph entirely in the browser's memory; every command shown elsewhere is
display-and-copy only. It is local-first (no accounts, no server database) and open
source under the MIT license.

Author: Kazi Musharraf (https://www.mkazi.live, https://github.com/mk-knight23).

Note on the name: "GitFlow" here is a brand for this learning platform, not the
nvie GitFlow branching model. The product teaches Git mechanics so users can pick
any workflow.

## Tools

- [Branch simulator](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/tool): in-memory Git graph engine (commit, branch, checkout, merge, rebase, reset) with an SVG graph, undo, and JSON export.
- [Command reference](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/reference): 40+ commands, each labeled safe/caution/destructive with examples and undo guidance.
- [.gitignore generator](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/gitignore): combine bundled templates into one deduplicated file, offline.
- [Commit builder](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/commits): compose Conventional Commit messages with live validation.
- [Undo helper](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/undo): match a mistake to a recovery recipe with risk-graded commands.
- [Repo analyzer](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/analyzer): score a public GitHub repo's docs health from public data only.
- [AI assistant](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/assistant): optional AI capabilities with honest availability states and deterministic fallbacks.

## Learn

- [Tutorials](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/tutorials): GitHub Desktop and command-line paths across three levels.
- [Quizzes](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/quiz): topic quizzes with per-question explanations.
- [Guides](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/guides): original long-form guides (reading the DAG, rebase vs merge, branching strategies, undoing anything, Conventional Commits, .gitignore, GitHub Desktop, CI triage).
- [Use cases](https://gitflow.mkazi.live/use-cases): onboarding juniors, teaching in a bootcamp, PR hygiene, recovering from mistakes, auditing repo health.
